tex_content.html:
There is more than one direction at ${\mathcal E}$.

Proof

\sketch Take a minimal geodesic ray $\gamma $ from a point $x$ limiting to the end and let $y$ be a point closer to ${\mathcal E}$ than $x$ and not lying on $\gamma $. Then a minimal geodesic ray from $y$ to ${\mathcal E}$ gives a direction at ${\mathcal E}$ distinct from the direction determined by $\gamma $.
